error_reason: The Planner agent repeatedly decides to have the WebSurfer agent open the exact same URLs (Laurence Olivier Wikipedia, DuckDuckGo search, Vivien Leigh Wikipedia) multiple times (Turns 1, 3, 5, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14) without actually scrolling the page to extract the information or changing the strategy despite the obvious failure of the action. This results in a rigid loop of identical steps that fails to progress the task.

suggested_fix.fix_text: The agent repeatedly reloads the Laurence Olivier Wikipedia page without scrolling to extract information. Implement a guard that forces the agent to scroll or specify a new search strategy after visiting the same URL 2-3 times without extracting new data, rather than defaulting to repeating the exact same navigation action.

probe_details.notes: The proposed error analysis correctly identifies a classic 'step_repetition' loop. The Planner explicitly notes that 'no spouse details have been extracted yet' on Turns 8, 10, and 12, yet instructs the WebSurfer to open the same URL ('https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laurence_Olivier') on Turns 7, 9, 11, and 13. The viewport remains fixed at 2% (top of page) on subsequent attempts, indicating a failure to scroll. The analysis accurately pinpoints the turns (1-14 range) and the specific URLs causing the deadlock. The reasoning is sound as the agents ignore their own observation of lack of progress.
